name: Almabtrieb mit Fest
beschreibung:
As summer draws to a close and the mountain meadows have been harvested, hundreds of cows, calves, sheep and goats make their way down from the high alpine pastures in the Lechtal. The Almabtrieb – the traditional cattle drive – is one of the most moving folk events in all of Tyrol. In mid-autumn, the village streets of the deeply carved Lechtal valley are transformed into a vibrant procession in which centuries-old tradition and farmer's gratitude are palpably felt.

Overview

The Almabtrieb usually takes place in the second to fourth week of September, with the exact date depending on weather, fodder and snowfall at altitude – often confirmed only at short notice. The largest Almabtrieb in the entire Tyrolean Außerfern is held by the local young farmers in Steeg, where cattle return from several high pastures including the Pimigalpe, Krabachalpe and Stieralpe. Events also take place in Bach, Elbigenalp (the „Duarfer Almabtrieb“), Holzgau and Stanzach.

The highlight is the “Aufkranzen” – decorating the lead cow and herd with spectacular headdresses of mountain pine boughs, alpine roses, dahlias and colourful ribbons, provided the summer passed without accident or loss. The cattle then parade through festively decorated village streets to the sound of cowbells and village brass bands. A farm market with regional products, wood carvings from Elbigenalp and Tyrolean specialities – Kiachla, Kasspatzln, Lechtal mountain cheese – await visitors in the festival tent.

Getting There

The Lechtal follows the B198 Lechtal road, reachable from Germany/north via Füssen/Reutte, from the Tyrolean Inn Valley via the Fernpass (B179) or the Hahntennjoch (L72) from Imst (no trailers allowed on the pass). During the main procession in Steeg (approx. 11:00–13:00), the B198 is fully closed. Arrive by 10:30 at the latest. By public transport: VVT line 110 (Reutte–Warth–Lech); rail travellers change at Reutte in Tirol.

Tips

  • Date: Check the exact date with the Lechtal Tourist Board (lechtal.at) or almabtrieb-steeg.at.
  • Families: Excellent – an unforgettable experience for children. Keep children away from the herd without adult supervision.
  • Dogs: Short lead only; the loud bells and crowds cause stress. Muzzle required on VVT buses.
  • Clothing: Sturdy footwear and weatherproof layers – the valley cools quickly in September.
